title: Probing of Dislocation-Controlled Domain Nucleation and Domain Wall Pinning in Single-Crystal BaTiO3 by MEMS-Based Multi-Stimuli In Situ (S)TEM
content: Engineering domain walls at the nanoscale presents a powerful strategy for enhancing the macroscopic functional properties of materials, unlocking new opportunities in electromechanics and electronics. This approach leverages imprinting topological defects into functional materials, which can significantly influence their performance and enable novel functionalities [1, 2]. However, despite its potential, a fundamental knowledge gap remains—from understanding fundamental pair interactions between dissociated topological dislocation cores [3] to their specific impact on domain nucleation and domain wall motion in ferroelectrics—posing a significant challenge. Addressing this is essential for further development and optimization of ferroelectric functional materials.
